settings.headline: Finance starts here
settings.subline: The finance club of IPM, IIM Ranchi. One repository, four learning paths and real stock pitches in front of real judges. Free for every student.

cfa.name: CFA & certifications
cfa.blurb: The credentials that finance recognises. Start with the CFA overview, then pick one certification and finish it.

val.name: Valuation & modeling
val.blurb: How a company is actually valued. Damodaran for the thinking, Wall Street Prep and Macabacus for the spreadsheet.

mkt.name: Markets & trading
mkt.blurb: Indian and global markets from zero. Zerodha Varsity first, then the data sources analysts use every day.

hard.name: Hard skills
hard.blurb: Excel, SQL, Python and Power BI. The tools that turn finance knowledge into work someone can use.

soft.name: Soft skills & communication
soft.blurb: Structure, negotiation and speaking. How to say the analysis so a room believes it.

read.name: Reading & listening
read.blurb: Letters, memos, podcasts and the books everyone in finance has read. Slow learning that compounds.

resources.d: Start here: levels, topic weights, registration windows and the scholarship routes most students miss.
The most-recommended free lecture series for Level I and II. Watch the ethics and quant playlists first.
Free study notes and a sample question bank per learning outcome. Good for quick revision before mocks.
The standard prep provider. Free sample QBank and the SchweserNotes format most candidates end up using.
The risk-management counterpart to the CFA. Worth it if you're headed to treasury, risk or trading desks.
India-specific, cheap and fast. Series VIII (Equity Derivatives) and XV (Research Analyst) are the useful ones for students.
resources.tags: nism sebi india research analyst derivatives

resources.d: An eight-hour e-learning cert on economics, currencies, fixed income and equities. Often free through the institute's terminal access.
The single most useful page on the internet for valuation. Lecture notes, data sets, industry betas, country risk premiums.
resources.tags: damodaran valuation dcf beta erp data

resources.d: Ready-made DCF, FCFE, option pricing and synthetic-rating models. Open one, break it, rebuild it.
resources.tags: damodaran excel template dcf fcfe model

resources.d: Full semester-length university courses recorded and posted free. Do the Valuation playlist over a summer.
The modeling course banks train analysts on. Their free knowledge base articles on LBO, DCF and comps are excellent on their own.
resources.tags: wsp modeling lbo dcf comps excel

resources.d: Free foundation courses on accounting, Excel and financial statements before you pay for anything.
Best-practice guides for DCF, LBO, merger and accretion models, with the formatting conventions banks expect.
The modeling tutorials most aspiring bankers start with. The free YouTube tutorials cover a surprising amount.
Ten years of financials for every listed Indian company, exportable to Excel. Your starting point for any Indian stock pitch.
resources.tags: screener india financials stock pitch export

resources.d: Read real 10-Ks and S-1s. Reading the MD&A of a company you like teaches more than most textbooks.

resources.t: Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies
resources.d: The reference text. Dense, but the chapters on ROIC and value drivers change how you read a balance sheet.
Step-by-step comps, precedent transactions, DCF and LBO exactly as done on a deal team.
The best free introduction to Indian markets. Modules on equities, technical analysis, options and personal finance.
resources.tags: varsity zerodha india options technical analysis

resources.d: When a term in a lecture goes over your head. Every concept explained in two paragraphs with an example.
Short, patient videos on interest, bonds, stocks, options and the 2008 crisis. Ideal if you're coming from a non-commerce background.
Live indices, option chains, bulk deals and historical data. Learn to read the option chain here before any derivatives course.
resources.tags: nse nifty option chain data india

resources.s: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
resources.d: Every macro series you'll ever cite, charted and downloadable. Yield curves, CPI, unemployment, money supply.
resources.tags: fred macro data yield curve cpi

resources.d: Monetary policy statements, the Database on Indian Economy, and the annual report that explains where India's money actually goes.
How Indian markets are regulated, how IPOs work, and what the rules actually say about insider trading.
Semester-length courses on financial markets, derivatives and corporate finance taught by IIT faculty. Free to audit, with an optional proctored certificate.
resources.tags: nptel swayam iit course india certificate

resources.d: Charting for everything. The free tier is enough to learn indicators and to build the charts for a pitch deck.
The derivatives textbook. Binomial trees, Black-Scholes, Greeks and the maths behind every structured product.
resources.tags: hull derivatives options black scholes greeks

resources.t: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
resources.d: The case for efficient markets, written for humans. Read it before you decide you can beat the index.
Every Excel function and shortcut with a worked example. Learn INDEX-MATCH, XLOOKUP and the keyboard-only workflow.
resources.tags: excel shortcuts functions xlookup index match

resources.d: Excel dashboards, Power Query and charts, taught by an Indian Excel expert who made it his career.
The friendliest SQL course, with a live editor. Enough for any analyst role that touches a database.
Python for economics and finance, from numpy to dynamic programming. Rigorous and free.
Four-hour micro-courses on Python, pandas and data visualisation. The fastest route from zero to a working notebook.
Official, free and structured. Corporate finance and FP&A roles increasingly ask for it.
Financial data, time series, portfolio optimisation and derivatives pricing in Python. For after Kaggle Learn.
resources.tags: python finance hilpisch time series portfolio

resources.d: What each finance role actually does, what it pays, and how people get in. Read the role guides first.
Structured problem solving for consulting-style cases, which is also how you should structure a stock pitch.
Answer first, then the reasons. The book behind every well-structured memo, deck and pitch.
Negotiation from an FBI hostage negotiator. Useful for deals, for negotiations, and for running a club.
A few free articles a month. Read the ones on presenting numbers, managing up and running meetings.
If you freeze in front of a room, this is the cheapest fix that works. Find a campus or city chapter.
Sixty years of plain-English lessons on capital allocation, moats and management. Start with 1977 and read forward.
Damodaran valuing whatever the market is arguing about this month, with the spreadsheet attached. Read one and you understand how a valuation argument is built.
Market cycles, risk and second-level thinking, in memos hedge fund managers actually read.
One Indian business or finance story a day, explained in three minutes. The easiest daily habit to build.
Long-form Indian equity research and the Three Longs & Three Shorts reading list, every week.
The pre-Budget document that explains the Indian economy in one place. Skim Volume 1 every January.
Three-hour histories of the great companies. Costco, Nvidia, LVMH. Case studies disguised as entertainment.
Long interviews with investors and operators. Listen for how they reason, not for the picks.
Mr. Market and margin of safety. Chapters 8 and 20 are the two that matter.
The original text on reading financial statements as an investor. Slow going, permanently useful.
Short essays on how people actually behave with money. The best first finance book to give anyone.
How to find companies before the analysts do, from the manager who returned 29% a year for thirteen years.
Salomon Brothers in the 1980s. The funniest and most honest account of what a trading floor is.
The rise and fall of Long-Term Capital Management. Leverage, models and what happens when both break.
Why the trader with the best track record may just be lucky. Read before you trust any backtest.
The RJR Nabisco LBO, told like a thriller. The best way to understand what private equity actually does.

paths.d: You've never bought a stock and the business news is noise. This gets you to fluent in a month.
paths.hint: Science or arts in school, no commerce background, no idea where to begin.

paths.d: Three statements to a defended DCF. What we'd want every member to finish over one summer break.
steps: Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies
paths.hint: I follow the news and can read a balance sheet. I want to value a company.

paths.d: The order that works around an IPM timetable. Ethics first, quant second, everything else in topic-weight order.
paths.hint: CFA Level I, planned around an IPM timetable.

paths.d: Know the roles, build the model, then learn to say it in the right order. The sequence behind a Bulls & Bears finalist.
paths.hint: Bulls & Bears: build the model, then defend it in front of a panel.

events.d: The flagship stock pitch. Long or short, one company, ten minutes, a panel that has heard every pitch before.
Three sessions from a three-statement model to a full DCF, built live in Excel on a real listed company.
Thirty minutes on what moved this week, why, and what the desk would have done about it.
Alumni across investment banking, research, asset management and corporate finance on what the first year actually looks like.

folders.d: The club's shared Drive: every folder and file members have added.
One-page finance CV templates, with the formatting the club recommends.
Technical and fit questions, grouped by role: banking, research, markets and corporate finance.
Sample cover letters and cold emails for finance roles.
Level I notes and formula sheets written by members who sat the exam.
Members' notes from IPM finance courses, club sessions and bootcamps.
DCF, comps and three-statement models built in club bootcamps.
Past Bulls & Bears decks and one-page models to learn the format from.
Slides and recordings from Market Wrap, Alumni Konnect and workshops.
